result.reasoning:
Could not refute. I reproduced the wrong output independently and root-caused it more precisely than the report did.

ROOT CAUSE (sharper than the report's "not always bit-identical"). `torch.nanquantile(x, 0.95, ...)` at /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/ops_ext.py:590 converts the Python float q to a scalar tensor of the INPUT's dtype. float32(0.95) = 0.949999988079071, so the rank is 0.949999988079071*240 = 227.99999713897705, NOT 228. floor = 227, so torch lerps from sorted[227] toward sorted[228] with weight 1-2.861e-6 and lands 2.861e-6*(sorted[228]-sorted[227]) BELOW sorted[228]. Proof the internal rank is < 228: on a float32 241-row, interpolation='lower' returns sorted[227] (1.7714053392410278), not sorted[228] (1.7796739339828491). For float64 input, 0.95*240 == 228.0 exactly in double, the rank is exact, and v == sorted[228] bit-exactly — which is why the float64 path is clean. Whether the float32 deficit survives rounding depends on the gap sorted[228]-sorted[227] relative to ulp(sorted[228]), which is why it fires on some days and not others.

REPRODUCTION (all in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/refute_es_boundary/, repo files untouched).
step1_mechanism.py — the report's trial 105 (default_rng(7), 500 draws, index 105). With 241 distinct values the q=0.95 linear quantile IS sorted[228] by definition, so "ABOVE" is exactly 12 minutes. torch float32 returns v = 1.3505467176437378 = sorted[228] - 1 ulp32, so |{x>v}| = 13 and day_es_ratio_hi = 1.5644932985305786 against the exact 1.6115342749466688 (2.92% error). torch float64, np.quantile float64 and np.quantile float32 all return sorted[228] exactly and give 12 minutes and the exact value. So the report's number and direction are right, and its "reference" is genuinely the correct quantity.
step2_systematic.py — v - sorted[228] in float32 ULPs over 500 draws: {0: 222, -1: 183, -2: 74, -3: 13, -4: 4, -5: 1, -6: 2, -7: 1}. Selected-set size histogram {12: 222, 13: 278}. Exactly matches the report's 278/500; so the admission is data-dependent, not a consistent off-by-one convention.
step3_production.py — through the real kernel, batched (200, 5, 241) float32 panels at the production geometry (float32 is declared "the production contract" in /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/engine/engine.py:85-101; n_minutes = 241 per the dt_meta.json files under tmp/review/verify/): Ret ~2e-3 581/1000 stock-days off by >1e-4 (median 1.20e-2, max 2.55e-2); lognormal Amt 695/1000 (median 3.03e-2, max 5.92e-2); t_4 ret 688/1000 (max 5.49e-2). float64 input: 0/1000, max error exactly 0.
step5_partial_days.py — not confined to M=241. The tie occurs whenever (n_finite - 1) % 20 == 0, i.e. n in {21,41,...,221,241}; measured 134-178/300 bad at n = 21, 41, 121, 201, 221, 241, with the error growing as n shrinks (max 3.35e-1 at n=21). Non-tie widths are clean (0/300 at n = 239, 240, 200).

REACHABILITY — this is live, not dead code. ops_ext is registered into AlphaCube's OPERATOR_REGISTRY at /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/bridge.py:46 and /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/idea_search.py:43, day_es_ratio_hi is in the NEW_OPERATORS export list (ops_ext.py:724), and it is an explicit U2 guidance template in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/alpha_distillation/B01_reverse_guidance.md:111 for the in-progress B01 batch.

TWO PLACES THE REPORT OVERSTATES (not enough to refute, but they shrink the blast radius):
1. Price-scale fields are immune. Close ~10.00 on a 0.01 tick: 0/1000 off by >1e-4 (max 1.82e-7), because 2.861e-6*gap falls below half an ulp when the gap is tiny relative to the level. The exposure is confined to zero-centred or wide-dynamic-range fields (Ret, Amt, Volume) — which is exactly what the docstring is written for, so it still matters.
2. day_es_ratio_lo is NOT clean, contrary to the report's "0/500" and its check_lo_mirror.py conclusion of a genuine code asymmetry. On lognormal Amt it fails 7/1000 (max 6.40e-2) and on t_4 ret 2/1000 (max 2.59e-2). It fails ~100x less because float32(0.05) = 0.0500000007450580597 errs UPWARD, giving a rank of 12.00000018 — an absolute deficit 16x smaller than q=0.95's — so it usually rounds back onto sorted[12]. That is a representation accident of the two literals, not a code asymmetry, and the fix must cover both branches.

Caveat on frequency only: I verified on synthetic panels, since the real minute store is on the server and off-limits. The production hit rate depends on how often a tradable day has all 241 minutes finite with distinct values bracketing the 95th order statistic. That does not affect the verdict — the kernel is demonstrably wrong against its own docstring at the production dtype and width — but the 56-70% rate is the synthetic rate, not a measured production rate.

result.corrected_fix:
The report's PRIMARY fix (float64 inside _es_ratio) is correct and I validated it, but its text needs two corrections and its "cheaper alternative" must be dropped.

(a) Validated fix, with the cast-back made load-bearing rather than incidental. In /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/ops_ext.py:587-596, widen at entry and narrow at exit so the quantile, the comparison AND the sums are all float64:

    def _es_ratio(x, q, hi):
        x0 = _f(x)
        out_dtype = x0.dtype
        x = x0.to(torch.float64)
        ok = torch.isfinite(x)
        v = torch.nanquantile(torch.where(ok, x, torch.full_like(x, NAN)), q, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        sel = ok & ((x > v) if hi else (x < v))
        k = sel.sum(-1)
        es = torch.where(sel, x, torch.zeros_like(x)).sum(-1) / k.clamp(min=1).to(x.dtype)
        v = v.squeeze(-1)
        good = (k > 0) & (v.abs() > 1e-8)
        return _day(es / torch.where(good, v, torch.ones_like(v)), good).to(out_dtype)

Measured: hi and lo both 0/1000 off by >1e-4 (max 5.9e-8) on Ret, Amt, t_4-Ret and Close. The `.to(out_dtype)` is mandatory, not polish: `_day` builds its NaN fill with `torch.full_like(v, NAN)`, so without it a float32 input yields a float64 day-value that then promotes every downstream float32 panel it touches, against the float32 production contract declared in AlphaCube's engine.py:85-101 (verified in step4_fix.py).

(b) DROP the report's "cheaper alternative" (a relative/ULP tolerance on the '>' / '<' comparison). It is unsound two ways: a multiplicative tolerance flips direction when v < 0, which is the normal case for day_es_ratio_lo and happens for hi on a down day; and it would also EXCLUDE genuine minutes that legitimately sit just above the quantile, trading a 1-ulp bug for a real-data bug.

(c) Note the residual fragility and prefer the dtype-independent variant if this is to be upstreamed. (a) works because 0.95*240 and 0.05*240 happen to round to exactly 228.0 and 12.0 in double; it is luck, not a guarantee, and the same class of defect returns for any (q, n) whose double product misses the integer. The version that does not depend on that luck computes the threshold itself from the integer finite-count: sort with NaNs pushed to the end, take n = ok.sum(-1, keepdim=True) as int64, form idx = q * (n - 1) in float64, and gather sorted[floor(idx)] and sorted[ceil(idx)] with the fractional weight — so an integer rank yields the order statistic bit-exactly by construction, for any input dtype.

(d) Fix both branches, not just hi. day_es_ratio_lo fails too (7/1000 on lognormal Amt, max 6.40e-2), just ~100x less often, so the report's framing of lo as a clean control should not be read as "only hi needs the change".

Out of scope but worth flagging to the coordinator: the same boundary pattern exists in AlphaCube's read-only legacy corpus, where the erm_* factors are written as is_gt(ret, day_quantile(ret, 0.95)) (/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/legacy/factor_set_merged.py:1320-1336). Those run through the same float32 day_quantile and are exposed to the same 241-minute tie; I did not verify them, and AlphaCube is read-only here.
